claims.statement: Offline validation retains immutable-owner OIDC tests. The owner-mail Graph PATCH is retired with state-only removal; read-only conversion tests reject the current federated target and require recovery administrator evidence. Live domain reconciliation, recovery sign-in, conversion, Fleet SAML and recovery login remain separate acceptance.

PR 1219's October 7, 2026 UTC plan initially failed on Harbor tuple reconciliation despite equal source counts and untainted state. Subsequent protected run37580800923 passed on861fb9d7 against427b01ad, including the aggregate gate, without a Harbor repair by this investigation. The separate reviewed owner-mail plan applied with fresh owner Octelium sessions verified before and after; the old SMTP alias remained secondary and the pilot rename was not retried. Strict CI gates remain intact.

Deluge's focused offline health test checks credential, RPC, timeout, malformed-status and disconnect failures with mocked Deluge/Twisted; deployed verification additionally requires bounded helper execution, cached VPN/RPC metrics and original-route acceptance.

Offline validation runs route and tokenless-kubeconfig fixtures, including exact LAN, bridge, and overlay /32 sources plus a dedicated no-token Renovate identity and Harbor host alias for registry port 9443; the separately invoked loopback runtime harness exercises declared Traefik routes and TLS reload. Neither replaces live ingress acceptance.
Rendered policy permits only three explicitly reviewed Tailscale Funnel Ingresses backed by the separate Traefik callback service and rejects other Funnel declarations.

Earlier cutover fixtures cover fixed DNS ownership, Mac credential preservation, bounded same-profile reconnect and rollback, callback preflights, and fresh delivery receipts. The current resolver handoff uses the observed tailnet DNS Service IP, direct UDP/TCP probes, owner restricted nameserver setting, and later normal client DNS and HTTPS acceptance.

The CI access checker verifies the scoped impersonated tag and allows an empty dry-run patch but requires the same real empty patch to be denied by the plan admission policy; apply mode checks administration permission without mutation.

Traefik scoped image publication retains digest, tag alias, and complete authenticated Harbor-pull verification with the dedicated reader, while Talos regression tests reject scoped, untitled, and mismatched-revision receipts as full-catalog evidence.

Private DNS readiness uses a transport-neutral parser for the final HTTP2 response, native +proto and gRPC-Web trailers, rejecting duplicate/conflicting statuses, earlier-response confusion and malformed bodies before DNS changes.

Offline validation runs fixed ingress-signer and CI-publisher fixtures, including fail-closed retirement and orphan recovery; real provider plan and readback remain required for production replacement.

The private DNS preflight accepts AFFiNE 500/502/503 and legacy OpenClaw 500/502 only with reviewed and live zero replicas; it requires deployed Traefik route/TLS parity and rejects other application 5xx responses. Retirement route checks cover the fixed 27 migration names, while the full check probes staged Enterprise routes with a matching Agent host and rejects edge 404.

PolicyBot's non-executing preflight requires hook HTTP404 with one valid 20-character backend X-Request-ID and root404 without that header; it checks routing, while fresh signed GitHub delivery remains required for callback acceptance.
Talos regression rejects divergent active/persistent full configuration streams and permits an absent persistent resource only for initial active version1.
CI signing regression requires three raw keys passed through stdin and excludes raw key values from argv and printed output.

The retained-connector regression requires exactly its octelium-client service-account principal and namespace/Pod selectors on private8443, rejecting unrelated identities and callback/registry ports.

Publisher regressions cover delayed and timed-out authority readback, durable pending receipt and cache replay, preview and retirement refusal with pending work, and exact orphan recovery that rejects nonempty or failed affected-signature lookup and unrelated trust drift.

The static wrapper verifies source-bound offline fixture and manifest-policy Nix outputs with protected-main cache trust, signatures and sandboxing before fresh remaining provider, network and security checks; cache reuse does not establish live plan or runtime acceptance.

Offline checks run mocked source-trust fixtures for pinned preparation, baseline retention, patch validation, bad hashes/roots, escaping symlinks, and nonempty contexts. The Linux candidate job declares read-only contents and non-persisted checkout credentials; it requires the original duplicate-reference failure, repaired tests, upstream API generation, and core compilation.

The Harbor candidate build runs isolated pinned Harbor/PostgreSQL services and a client sharing the proxy network namespace to verify unchanged repeated-index and complete blob push/pull with exactly one database relation. Offline fixtures validate payload hashes, refuse upload locations outside the loopback endpoint and require no published host ports, internal networking and core health ordering.

The candidate build runs the complete CSRF middleware tests and ten browser/session compatibility cases against the replacement dependency with networking disabled; cases require valid same-origin requests and legacy headers, deny cross-site/same-site browser requests and preserve the non-session API exemption. The middleware unit tests use in-memory configuration without their former unused PostgreSQL bootstrap.

The candidate build adds a native JWK trust attack regression and a compiled-package graph guard against OpenPGP and Distribution proxy/storage/handler server packages. These specific advisory-prerequisite checks retain unfiltered module-level findings and do not replace final-container/component scans.

Offline Harbor fixtures accept legacy JSON and current blob-path Docker-save config layouts. They distinguish archive config path/byte hash mismatch from inspected root descriptor mismatch; containerd fixtures verify an index root or direct manifest and reject wrong root, wrong selected config and corrupt root blob. They reject wrong Grype raw config hash or reported image ID, platform/distro, invalid or stale databases, filtering/exclusions and available fixes while retaining unresolved findings. Receipts omit raw metadata and deny CVE clearance. The Linux job runs unit checks and a private runtime audit after a non-persisted checkout.

Core publication fixtures enforce one fixed subject, dedicated workflow/current-main binding, full private pull/digest verification before signing, enrolled-key verification, Harbor-only signer images, and withheld outputs on failure. The protected publisher requires zero matches in the exact full-container Grype report before registry credentials; ordinary audit fixtures retain unresolved findings. Static credential-job inventory and canonical workflow hashes enroll the publisher/reporting jobs; these source tests do not dispatch publication.

Harbor publication regressions include a native offline Skopeo test using generated local OCI fixtures with network transports rejected, requiring original root and both platform-child manifest digests and repeated descriptors to survive directory staging and a second copy; this does not prove Harbor publication, signature accessories or live consumers.

The Harbor Core publication workflow runs the pinned public Chainguard Cosign compatibility fixture before AWS credential configuration, and validate runs the same fixture. It checks disposable P-256 import, OpenSSL public-key equality and producer signing flags. The dated October 11 reviewer observation is historical; current source declares automatic same-repository PR-plan and production environments, with production restricted to exact main. Live settings require fresh verification.

The Linux Nix builder retains NET_ADMIN for private loopback with disabled host user namespaces; its Pod-networking authority restricts submissions to reviewed source. The manifest selects the dedicated deny-by-default Localhost profile only for the nix container while retaining Pod RuntimeDefault, sandbox/signature enforcement, the 1 GiB reservation/limit, serial substitutions and original-Pod/attempt-ID cancellation. Both eligible worker profiles must be verified before selection rollout; each publication attempt checks node health, fresh leases/metrics and at least 1.5 GiB measured headroom. Rendered/deployed source alone does not prove full-check capacity or signed cache substitution.

Offline validation runs credential-materializer fixtures that reject unsafe files/directories, stale main, inherited AWS credentials and proxies, and private-value leaks. Talos fixtures limit registry auth to robot$mirror+pull, reject unrelated Harbor auth, and remove only their owned entry on rollback. An executable ordinary mirror rollout requires supplied reader auth unless its captured configuration already has owned reader auth; a missing credential stops before Harbor receipt checks, candidate machine-config rendering, or apply-config. The fixtures do not read SSM or mutate nodes.

The dedicated Nix builder seccomp declaration preserves the captured containerd 2.1.4 amd64 builder rules and adds only pivot_root with a deny-by-default action. Its node-scoped helper preserves other profiles and active/persistent configuration, requires exact reviewed main for execution, rejects configuration/boot drift, validates strictly and verifies no-reboot installation through bounded asynchronous readback of /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/profiles without repeating apply. Rollback refuses a selected profile and requires exact-path file-not-found readback, not transport/authentication failure. Nine tests cover baseline hash, idempotence, conflicts, configuration races, selected-profile refusal, delayed pinned-path readback, wrong content, deadline and deletion discrimination. The runbook records the initial worker0 legacy-path readback failure and subsequent protected repair: worker0 was verified read-only and worker1's first released helper succeeded, with both exact file hashes and unchanged boots. The current manifest declares container-only Localhost selection after those file receipts, retains Pod RuntimeDefault, and requires separate Argo/OCI verification and separately released bounded publication; no cache acceptance follows from source alone.

The dated runbook preserves the initial exact6dd7 rollout/headroom hold and subsequent successful bounded signed publication of both Linux checks, independent signature acceptance/rejections, cleanup and905MiB peak/noOOM. Exactmain warmCI38349343865 attempt2 repojob115167993774 copied both published outputs without rebuilding and passed remaining freshvalidation. Cache proof applies to exact6dd7 source; laterdocs change fingerprints. Separately freshplan-only38506080728 exactsigned12eaf629/base0a442055 livejob115665635536 and policygate passed APIproxychecks and Terraformplanning; independentclusterchecks found allfourReady/no pressure/originalbuilderReady1Gi/Argohealthyatbase. Migrationapply,retirement and furthercachepublication remainheld; docsmerge releases none.

Mastodon offline fixtures cover launcher, owner bootstrap, routing, SMTP injection and DNS conflict handling, while protected live activation additionally requires declared registration, real workload health, provider delivery and public behavior; the DNS lane installs and uses its pinned Nix shell.

The validate workflow retains a disposable dual-stack Kind NRI enforcement fixture for pull requests and main pushes. It checks baseline, startup denial, allowed Service/DNS traffic, connection revocation and denial while the worker process is paused. This legacy fixture is separate from the staged, dormant kube-router firewall path and does not qualify its canary or prove production enforcement.

The fixed Harbor 2.15.4 publication scope contains exactly nine digests from the reviewed full catalog; publisher fixtures reject unreviewed scope entries and require selected-image pull verification. Scoped success does not prove full-catalog acceptance; the revised 214-image catalog passed protected all run 40011909180.

The registry pre-pull fixture checks that dry-run mode avoids mutation, execution verifies exact reviewed main, cached digests are skipped, changed scope is rejected, and a pull without the expected cache alias fails. Live acceptance still requires both reviewed registry pins cached on all four Talos nodes immediately before the Harbor consumer merge.

The pinned Langfuse chart render requires one web replica with no explicit strategy, a 1280 MiB request, unchanged 2 GiB limit, and required Acer affinity. The capacity receipt is a projection; live acceptance requires the replacement web Pod Ready on Acer, the old Pod gone from zimaboard-1, recovered SQL/web behavior, and fresh node headroom and pressure readback.

The bounded Nix builder attempt at af18e0e6 failed at sandbox pivot_root before offline checks or signed publication; cleanup and node health were independently verified, and any profile recovery required separate approval.

The image-policy CI job verifies the shipped Warn and Audit binding admits public images with warnings, and tests Deny only in a disposable Kind fixture; live audit and authenticated Harbor/node pulls remain required before production Deny.

Cordium runner source checks cover fixed builds, JIT provisioning, credential refresh, UID network policy, controller access, and cleanup, but live NRI enforcement, cold pulls, canary, and workflow acceptance remain required before registration or selector cutover.

The fixed Renovate scope contains eight reviewed catalog digests, including the runner. Publisher fixtures reject unreviewed entries and exercise selected-image copy and authenticated pull behavior; the credentialed workflow exact hash locks the reviewed fixed scopes.

Harbor publisher transport fixtures require exact-error OCI conversion fallbacks for destination upload and a resumed alias copy, with unchanged root digest and alias plus a complete authenticated pull; generic destination failures remain terminal. These fixtures do not prove live full-catalog publication.

The repository's local validation entry point is `nix run .#validate`; the flake app generates the Terragrunt stack before HCL formatting and validation, static checks, and Conftest policies. Focused docs checks and live plan or rollout acceptance remain separate.

Native Chainguard receipt fixtures use Skopeo with generated local OCI indexes to prove complete two-platform and repeated-descriptor copies, and require Harbor's exact vulnerability report header. The static gate rejects status-write grants in pull-request workflows; these checks do not dispatch the protected receipt.

The tailnet DNS resolver gate renders the pinned chart and checks route/annotation parity and fixed 27-name initial migration. A protected scoped Harbor run must prove the pinned image digest and authenticated pull. After GitOps health, the signed DNS proxy and direct UDP/TCP 53 handoff checker bind the observed Service IP to all approved names while preserving public fallback and apex records; owner DNS and client acceptance remain separate.

The staged Renovate runner has static config and discovery checks plus offline Prometheus fixtures for missed starts, incomplete cycles, late prior success, suspension and resume just before an hour boundary, and a missing CronJob. Its first post-resume slot alerts after the 15-minute start grace; the completion alert's 56-minute threshold exceeds the 15-minute start allowance plus 40-minute Job runtime. These checks do not establish live credential, cache, or scheduled-Job acceptance.
The Renovate config fixture simulates a cache write failure and requires the runner to stop before any GitHub API request; this does not prove live PVC failure handling.
The pinned Renovate 44.167.4 local cache fixture verifies rebuilding missing and malformed package and repository cache entries; live PVC-failure recovery and seven-day acceptance remain pending.

Feature 005 separates 26 public app subdomain retirement targets from 29 current private resolver names, preserving the fixed first 27 migration routes as the retirement HTTPS gate. Before any DELETE, the helper scans the complete Cloudflare zone and fails closed on relevant child NS delegation or an out-of-set covering wildcard A/AAAA/CNAME. It checks authoritative answers and rereads full target fields so drift blocks deletion; per-name caller, DNS-01, preserved-record, post-TTL absence, and private access gates remain required.

The fixed LiteLLM scope selects one reviewed Linux amd64 child digest, while the consumer source now pins that child and the catalog excludes the failing root index. Coverage and publisher fixtures reject missing, altered, or extra scope entries before credentials; the shared publisher verifies source manifest bytes and a fresh complete authenticated Harbor pull. Protected run 39210811031 passed one-image publication, but it does not prove full-catalog coverage.

The OpenClaw Enterprise model-credential workflow binds to exact current main and validates an owner-supplied OpenRouter key before writing only its distinct SSM path; no key is supplied. Stopped legacy inventory, off-NAS archive publication, separate multi-root restore verification, and protected 214-image catalog publication passed. Isolated canary, platform upgrades, compatible legacy boot and new-state restore remain acceptance gates.

The protected OpenClaw Enterprise platform workflow wires fixed Talos and Kubernetes upgrade stages through an exact-main executor that checks private prerequisite readback, node role and disk preservation, and pinned Harbor tags; activation and canary node remain unset, so source fixtures do not establish live NetworkPolicy enforcement or authorize upgrades.

The dormant Enterprise foundation is rendered in static validation to check restricted namespaces, tenant RoleBindings, exact OnChange SSM projections, PostgreSQL certificate shape, ingress denial and disabled activation; this does not prove live readiness.

Enterprise reconciler fixtures in static and offline validation check stable Installation and workload snapshots, source-bound journaled Namespace/Configuration/stopped-Agent reconciliation, and read-only verification without inference. A staged one-shot operator dispatcher, retained journal claim, and clean-source non-root operator image recipe are source-validated. Protected publisher run 40056484158 signed and fully pulled all four images from exact source fda0d68, and the selected operator digest/source SHA are pinned in the disabled declaration. Absent static PV placement, admitted node and proved bootstrap-key ownership still block live dispatch.

Enterprise attestation compares nonempty resource versions for an immutable Installation Secret and each Deployment, ReplicaSet and Pod across two read-only snapshots, rejecting workload races with unchanged UIDs.

Enterprise API access pins the bootstrap key destination to the exact console origin, and activation validation accepts only the approved OpenRouter transport/model fields and dedicated model-key reference; offline fixtures reject altered inputs.

The staged OpenClaw Enterprise private-access fixtures validate a scoped authenticated Octelium console and redirect, an exact 32-hex native Agent route through private Traefik, WebSocket and lookalike-host behavior, and explicit console and Agent certificate SANs; source checks do not establish live access.

Dormant Enterprise chart validation renders the pinned chart and reviewed Installation profile; offline fixtures test the fixed immutable startup Secret and bounded hook behavior without qualifying live Pod binding.

Checkov secrets scanning uses an exact four-finding baseline for three non-secret public Kubernetes Secret-name strings in dormant Enterprise chart source and one generated octeliumee-secretman NetworkPolicy name paired with its reviewed spec hash; the static gate rejects a wider baseline.

A Namespace reconciliation retry recovers an uncertain create only from a unique exact API candidate; ready acceptance requires exact API and owned Kubernetes readback with the three pinned base NetworkPolicies. A blocked run may already have changed state, and removal requires a reviewed logical-Namespace cleanup path.

Harbor publication fixtures require a transient destination alias lookup to recover on retry, while an authorization failure stops the lookup without retry; fixture success does not prove protected publication.
The validate whitespace step diffs the pull-request base or push before SHA against HEAD, using the empty tree for a new-branch push, so changed lines are checked on a clean checkout.

The n8n AI migration check exercises the staged one-time Job with synthetic exports and proves the active deployment excludes the migration. It covers exact conversions, inactive and idempotent behavior, credential preservation, absent or edited target nodes, and rejection of listing/export, malformed-data, duplicate-node and write failures without blocking app startup.

T017 accepted an 18:00 UTC scheduled Renovate full dry-run Job covering all eight eligible owner repositories after the 17:00 datasource mutex timeout; effective writes and full owner/App parity remain separate gates.

The offline static gate renders all nine DNS egress policies, requires TCP and UDP port 53 peers to select only kube-system Pods labeled k8s-app=kube-dns, and checks the exact kube-dns Service and CoreDNS Deployment Pod selectors; live canary DNS qualification remains pending.

The read-only NetworkPolicy inventory compares normalized ingress and egress rules, fails on missing, drifted, or source-only policies, and labels mixed or policy-type-transition drift direction-neutrally. Omitted or empty policyTypes defaults to Ingress, with Egress added only for nonempty egress rules; older private review hashes need refresh.

Offline peer regression checks Cloudflared origins and gateway selectors, Harbor monitoring peers, Harbor and Mastodon ingressgateway peers, and Mastodon's ambient HBONE TCP/15008 allowance. These source checks do not prove traffic through an enforcing dataplane.

The protected private Octelium catalog job supplies a read-scoped GitHub token to its fixed helper, which selects exactly three Policies and three Services and rechecks the current main SHA immediately before each of two catalog writes. Missing or advanced main stops the next write, and offline fixtures cover both stale-SHA points and lookup failure; these source checks do not prove a live dispatch.

Offline Harbor publication fixtures require an OCI-index authenticated pull to recover after four classified transport failures in one temporary OCI directory while retaining partial content, forcing recursive checks of nested data, and using bounded backoff. They report exhaustion after five attempts and stop on hard failures.

The staged homelab-ci-plan Octelium workload policy permits Kubernetes read verbs and dry-run writes while denying live writes and subresources; offline fixtures exercise these declared rules, but source checks do not establish live enforcement or issue a plan credential.

The 19:00 and 20:00 scheduled Renovate dry runs hit the same public canary datasource key on distinct Pods; after protected v0.0.2 publication, the 21:00 scheduled run refreshed that record and selected one new canary branch proposal, completing T022.

Retained 17:00 logs identified one repository's lookup errors and the Job/alerts failed visibly; the protected 03:00 missed-slot drill fired RenovateHourlyCycleMissing at 03:20:47, and the restored 04:00 scheduled Job succeeded with alert clearance, completing T045.

The 2026-10-20 13:07–13:15 UTC post-shutdown read-only recheck leaves T022 blocked: the best worker has about 3,398 MiB unreserved versus a 4,096 MiB initial Enterprise steady request, 6,308 MiB actual use and 9.74 GB root-filesystem space free. Every worker has less than 10.74 GB for a new 10 GiB local claim under the existing /var/lib pattern; acer has only 1,802 MiB unreserved versus the 2,304 MiB database-plus-gateway minimum, and unrelated Pods prevent NoSchedule taint isolation.

The protected PR plan fails when AzureAD stack or shared root sources or plan inputs change and the plan environment lacks client/tenant selectors or a complete GitHub OIDC session; unrelated changes may skip AzureAD.
The PR static job fails before deciding to skip the live Terragrunt plan if it cannot read the base diff, and an offline fixture exercises that failure.

The protected owned-cleanup stage loads the approved immutable firewall-ownership receipt under the current source SHA and follows its evidenceSourceSha to the original placement receipt under the evidence SHA. Each exact key requires an untruncated single latest version without delete markers, KMS encryption, a 1-byte to 1-MiB object length, and a matching SHA-256 checksum on the version-pinned download before cleanup-attempt or firewall access; live cleanup remains disabled.

Read-only fixtures bind complete expected NetworkPolicy specs for three pinned Cordium v0.12.7, four pinned Octelium v0.35.0 Genesis, and ten pinned Octelium Enterprise policies; all 17 are source-bound, but pinned generator-binary rendering and live enforcement remain unverified.

Pinned Cordium ws-main and Octelium svc-upstream constructors hardcode public IPv4 and IPv6 egress on all ports without a public-egress input; additive NetworkPolicies cannot narrow either rule. A reviewed upstream patch or fork, rebuilt and pinned images, actual generator renders, and isolated canary traffic and private-range denial qualification are required before enforcement.

The protected Enterprise workflow has fixed binding and runtime stages with exact-current-main checks, a shared production queue, and pinned helpers. The full-sync helper now rechecks current main after final Argo health readback, and an offline race fixture requires a blocked outcome when main advances during sync. Binding lacks hosted delivery of the owner-controlled 0600 key; full-sync remains blocked by the unselected installation phase; reconcile, stop, and verification have exact-main one-shot Job dispatch but the disabled operator gate stops before creation, while restore and acceptance remain separately blocked.

Production Terragrunt apply rechecks current main before direct imports, untaints, Kubernetes writes, and applies; the root before_hook checks each multi-unit apply and the bootstrap after_hook checks before each self-management manifest write, failing closed on stale or unreadable main.

Canary admission requires a complete cluster-wide selector inventory with no labeled Node before mutation and immediately before labeling; after the patch it verifies only the configured Node and rolls back its own label on conflict while retaining the isolation taint.

Canary release removes the selector label and waits for every cleanup DaemonSet Pod to disappear across the cluster. It then requires a complete canary-node Pod inventory matching only reviewed system DaemonSet UIDs before removing the isolation taint; a surviving cleanup Pod, incomplete inventory, changed Pod, or timeout keeps the taint.

The static gate runs Installation binder fixtures for exact-main checks, stable Ready-controller and returned-ID proof, a UID/resource-version guarded Secret annotation patch, and idempotent readback. A protected fixed binding lane is declared but requires an owner-controlled 0600 private service-key file with no hosted-runner delivery; no live binding has occurred.

The dormant PostgreSQL 18 fixture runs pinned upstream migration 0008 as the migrator, checks TLS 1.3 and role boundaries, and proves the app role can access its migrated auth table without schema creation or access to a new ungranted table; live storage and restore remain pending.

The source-only Enterprise active lifecycle fixtures cover key-file permissions, exact Agent grant, first and second Configuration generations, guarded native-origin revision, uncertain deployment and stop responses, and read-only verification of both revisions; committed activation remains disabled, so no live acceptance follows.

T014 legacy compatibility rehearsal remains partial after protected resume-restore run 40050057926 prepared a separate verified private NAS scratch recovery tree. Six external NAS symlinks point to five nonempty pinned-image directories, but the former writable overlay is unclassified and three absent external /home targets plus an already-dangling NAS skill link need disposition. A writable UID 1000 local-state copy and old-image boot behind enforced offline isolation remain required while original claims stay read-only.

Ownership capture, approval, cleanup and release refuse a live network-policy-canary Namespace or remaining fixture workload and require a complete assigned canary-node Pod inventory matching reviewed system DaemonSet namespace/name/UID identities plus the validated cleanup Pod while it runs. Release rechecks only those reviewed system identities after cleanup Pod deletion; a restarted system Pod blocks the immutable placement path pending separately reviewed recovery.

The source-only Kubernetes maintenance stage checks live Istiod, CNI, ztunnel, and both injected gateways before upgrade and after verification. It requires reviewed digest-bearing Istio 1.30.6 images and fully observed, ready controllers that are not marked for deletion, including Deployment total replicas equal to desired so old terminating replicas block the stage. Matching mutable tags are rejected. T025 must align chart image hubs and digest-bearing injection with the reviewed catalog; no live upgrade has run.

The Platform Maintenance policy accepts only workflow_dispatch, requires explicit empty workflow permissions, and binds both jobs. A shared rule rejects workflow and job run defaults or environment, step shell and working-directory overrides, and BASH_ENV or ENV on any step. Regression fixtures cover trigger and run-setting changes; this source gate does not establish live maintenance readiness.

The protected Enterprise Startup Candidate and Enterprise Operations policy rules require workflow_dispatch as their sole event and share a run-setting guard that rejects unreviewed defaults, environment, shell and working-directory settings. The credentialed legacy stage requires an exact eight-variable environment. Regression fixtures cover reusable triggers and shell-prelude overrides; these checks do not prove live execution.

The Enterprise registration fixture renders both generated Applications, verifies disabled automatic sync and the scoped AppProject, and compares pinned chart resources with the allowlist when upstream source is available; it does not prove live application or sync.

Harbor publisher fixtures require fixed Enterprise preflight, per-image pull, signing, and cleanup failure phases while withholding private output; passing offline fixtures does not replace a successful protected four-image publication receipt.

The Enterprise recovery fixture exercises unknown stop intent, interrupted runtime reads, and preservation of the separate legacy archive after a new-Agent stop failure; it runs in the static gate but supplies no live restore receipt.

Protected publication run 39466313228 completed bounded multipart upload but failed in the former broad publication-version phase; that attempt produced no final receipt. The reviewed helper now reports fixed public pre- and post-upload phases while withholding private diagnostics. A later source-bound publication passed.

A read-only 2026-10-20 21:00 UTC recheck found all nodes Ready and untainted, no worker with 10 GiB free for one new local claim, Acer below the database-plus-gateway memory request, and unrelated Pods without canary tolerations. T022, T027, and T035 remain blocked with no live admission.

The static registration fixture accepts only five reviewed policy/canary GitOps source phases and rejects mixed sync or manifests. Protected maintenance fetches full Git history and verifies first-parent ancestry from the qualified evidence SHA through two dedicated prune commits to current main, accepting unrelated commits but rejecting intervening changes in operational source roots and Nix flake inputs. Current-SHA private ownership and cleanup receipts remain required.

Harbor publication fixtures require transient HTTP 5xx Skopeo and OCI-index authenticated reads to recover on bounded retry; persistent OCI-index 5xx reports server-error after five attempts, while HTTP 404, auth, missing-content and digest failures stop without retry.

Detached archive run 39366476872 produced the private source result. Protected publish-archive run 39501240221 used that result and passed versioned off-NAS upload, restore, archive verification and private final receipt. Later runs 39700564687 and 39908653791 used the publication as an archive-worker reference and failed before upload. Separate verify run 39910018168 succeeded against the exact publication reference, restoring both versioned objects and verifying full local/NAS content and both SQLite databases; T013 is complete.

The corrected 2026-10-23 placement check keeps T022 and T035 blocked: Embedded OpenClaw uses one 1,792 MiB Gateway on the agents selector with a 10 GiB local state claim, without a separate 768 MiB Harness Pod. Only acer has local disk for the Gateway and database claims, but their 2,304 MiB floor is 502 MiB above its 1,802 MiB unreserved memory; the 4,096 MiB co-located planning budget and isolated worker canary remain unadmitted.

The Harbor core failure-status fixture covers a failed scan stage, fixed identity categories including archive self-hash, inspected root descriptor, descriptor graph, Grype report config and reported image ID, a remediation category and malformed status. Validate prints only an allowlisted stage/category or unknown while retaining the full private log and failing the job.

The offline Enterprise recovery fixture executes the backup preflight and rejects false, missing, empty-UID, malformed, and concatenated writer markers while accepting one valid stopped-writer object; this does not attest live PVC identity, a sustained writer fence, or scheduled off-node backup.

The offline static gate requires all six declared Istio chart sources to use the replacement blob.istio.io chart URL with unchanged 1.27.3 revisions and automated self-heal, while the separate 1.28.10 candidate remains disabled with pinned archive hashes.

The Istio runbook declares the replacement chart repository for active 1.27.3 sources and inventories without changing versions or package hashes. A scoped Terragrunt apply and unchanged-image Argo health readback remain required, and the old GCS AppProject entry is retained for rollback until verification.

The source-only Enterprise stop and stopped-state verification require an unfiltered raw namespaced Kubernetes PodList with a resource version, no continuation page, and no items after OCE reports termination; any Pod or uncertain list blocks, and the staged operator has only namespace-scoped pods/list for this proof.

Protected prepare-restore runs 39942297939, 39951803625 and 39966041305 failed before receipt download and restore-worker execution. A source diagnostic repair exposed fixed public source-range, reader-transfer and finalization subphases without private diagnostics. The exact-version range helper checks metadata, transfers SHA-256-verified slices with rollback and no-clobber promotion; focused fixtures cover damaged ranges and interrupted transfers. Later guarded resume-restore run 40050057926 passed prior-job provenance, verified cached archive and receipt, and prepared a separate private NAS scratch recovery tree. T014 still requires an isolated old-image boot.
Offline inventory and publisher fixtures pin the one-image Prometheus qualification scope to the exact full-catalog digest and reject altered or extra entries before credentials.

Destination-copy fixtures require fixed public categories for Skopeo blob and manifest write errors, keep HTTP 5xx as server-error, and leave unknown errors terminal without private diagnostic leakage.

Full mirror run 39906968373 stopped at pinned Prometheus item 196 of 214 and produced no complete receipt; one-image qualification alone cannot pass the full-catalog gate. Later protected all run 40011909180 passed all 214 reviewed images with matching digests and complete authenticated Harbor pulls.
